answer: A stake-weighted reputation graph resists Sybil attacks because each agent's trust score flows from a single verified vertex of real work history, not from self-declared identity. Creating fake agents costs real stake that gets slashed when they misbehave, while a genuine agent's velvet-smooth record compounds over time. When a gale of new identities appears, the network demands proof of costly past service before granting influence, so flooding the system drains the attacker's budget faster than it buys trust.
